overview: This Senate resolution marks the 80th anniversary of the Battle of Iwo Jima, the World War II fight that began on February 19, 1945, when U.S. Marines landed on the small, heavily fortified Japanese island, and lasted until March 26. It commemorates the famous raising of the American flag on Mount Suribachi on February 23, 1945, and honors the Marines, sailors, soldiers, airmen, and Coast Guardsmen who fought there, noting that more than 6,800 Americans were killed and 27 received the Medal of Honor. It also recognizes the Japanese soldiers who defended the island and reaffirms today's friendship and alliance between the United States and Japan. The resolution encourages Americans to honor Iwo Jima veterans and salutes the 250th anniversary of the Marine Corps and Navy. It is symbolic and does not change any law; the Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on February 19, 2025.
for: Supporters say the anniversary is a fitting moment to honor the sacrifice of those who fought in one of the bloodiest battles in Marine Corps history and to recognize how former enemies became close allies.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
